title: Surgery for a herniated disc
what: A surgeon removes the part of the disc that presses on a nerve. It is usually done through a small cut in the back, under general anesthesia.
why: When strong pain in the leg or arm does not go away after treatment without surgery, or with leg weakness. Urgently, if you lose control of your bladder or bowels.
duration: the surgery usually takes 1 to 2 hours; the hospital stay is usually 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. The doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes
If you or your relatives ever had problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: A spine MRI, blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a check by a general doctor. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the evening before, and no drinks for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: It is better to quit beforehand. Wounds and the disc heal better.

prepare.title: Things to pack
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, shoes without laces, a phone charger, and the medicines you take every day.

bring: Your MRI: images and the report
Your ID and a list of your medicines
Things for a 1 to 3 day hospital stay
steps: On the day of surgery, you change into a gown, and a cannula is put into a vein
In the operating room, the anesthesiologist gives the medicine, and you fall asleep
You are placed on your stomach
The surgeon makes a small cut and, using a microscope, removes the part of the disc pressing on the nerve
The cut is closed, and you wake up in the recovery room
feel: Pain at the cut. You will get pain medicine
Leg pain often gets better right away. Numbness may take weeks to go away
after: You are usually allowed to get up and walk the same day or the next day
For a few weeks, do not lift heavy things, bend suddenly, or sit for a long time
Your surgeon will say when you can drive and go back to work
Exercise therapy as your doctor prescribes
Your surgeon will say if the stitches need removing or will dissolve
red_flags: A fever over 38 degrees, or redness or fluid coming from the wound
New weakness or numbness in your legs
Losing control of your bladder or bowels, or numbness in the groin: call emergency services right away
A strong headache that gets worse when you stand up

faq.q: Can the herniated disc come back after surgery?
faq.a: Sometimes yes, in a small number of people. The risk is lower if you protect your back, do not smoke, and do your exercises.

faq.q: Does a herniated disc always need surgery?
faq.a: No. Most often it is treated without surgery. Surgery is offered when treatment does not help or the nerve is badly affected.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. Pack your things, MRI, ID, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time your clinic gave you.
